full_judgment:
7. The trial Court on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence arrived at the finding that defendant Nos. 1-9's predecessor Abdul Hamid on the basis of the deed of reconveyance got the land sold on July 26, 1960 reconveyed in the year 1961. The trial Court noticed the fact that in the deed (Exhibit 1 dated July 26, 1960) whereby Abdul Hamid sold the land in suit to Abdur Razzaque, plot No.8276 was mentioned but in the agreement for reconveyance executed by Abdur Razzaque, in favour of Abdul Hamid on that very day i.e. July 26, 1960 (Exhibit Gha 2) and in the kabala (Exhibit Ga 9 dated May 15, 1961) whereby Abdur Razzaque, reconveyed the land which he purchased on July 26, 1960, from Abdul Hamid, plot number was mentioned as 8275, but in the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case the trial Court arrived at the finding that the mistake in Exhibit Gha(2) and Ga(9) was an inadvertent mistake of the scribe although khatian number and the other description of the land as well as the quantity of land has been written correctly and, as such, held that as Abdur Razzaque reconveyed the land on May IS, 1961 to the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-9 and since then he having had no right, title and interest which he acquired by the kabala dated July 26, 1960, the plaintiff by purchase from Abdur Razzaque by the kabala dated May 11, 1978 (Exhibit 2) has not acquired any right, title, interest and possession in the land in suit. The trial Court on detailed discussion of the evidence of PWs 1 and 2 who deposed on behalf of the plaintiff held that plaintiff inisetably failed to prove her possession in the land in suit. It may be mentioned plaintiff or any of her sons or relatives did not depose in the suit. Plaintiff tried to establish her right, title and possession in the land in suit through the evidence of PW 1, the constituted attorney and PW 2, the servant of the plaintiff but their evidence being contradictory was not accepted by the trial Court and also did not consider them as reliable witnesses to prove the case of the plaintiff. 

 12. The undenied position is that land in suit belonged to Abdul Hamid and he transferred the same to Abdur Razzaque on 26-7-1960. It is the case of the contesting defendants that on 26-7-1960 Abdur Razzaque executed and registered a deed of reconveyance in favour of Abdul Hamid regarding the transfer made by Abdul Hamid to Abdur Razzaque from whom plaintiff claimed to have purchased the land in suit on May 11, 1978. It is also the case of the defendants that pursuant to the deed of reconveyance Abdur Razzaque re-conveyed the land in suit to Abdul Hamid on May 15, 1961. The defendants have contended that although in the agreement for reconveyance plot number was incorrectly written 8275 instead of 8276, land whereof was sold by Abdul Hamid to Abdur Razzaque on 26-7-1960 followed by an agreement for reconveyance and thus when Abdur Razzaque reconveyed the land on May 15, 1961 mistake that occurred in the agreement for reconveyance crept into the deed executed by Abdur Razzaque in favour of Abdul Hamid in respect of the Iand in suit but on the basis of reconveyance the defendants are in possession of the land in suit which is of plot No. 8276. It has also been contended by the defendants that the other descriptions of the land i.e. khatian, mouza, quantity of land etc. were quite correct or, in other words, uniform to that of deed of sale dated 46-7-1960. This contention of the defendants though was considered correct by the trial Court but was not accepted by the appellate Court upon referring to the provision of section 91 of the Evidence Act and the High Court Division concurred with the lower appellate Court. The Iearned Advocate of the appellant submits that in the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record, provision of section 91 of the Evidence Act was in no way relevant for consideration or, in other words, provision of section 91 of the Evidence Act had no manner of application in the background of the case put forward by the parties. The submissions so made merits consideration in the context of the frame of the suit.
